headline_marked: DP World to [[operate Chittagong Port's New Mooring Container Terminal]]
headline: DP World to operate Chittagong Port's New Mooring Container Terminal
summary: A concession agreement was signed on Thursday despite protests from leftist political parties and port workers.
details: A concession agreement has been signed with Dubai-based DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) at Chittagong Port. The signing ceremony took place on Thursday at the Invest Bangladesh Auditorium in Agargaon, Dhaka.

The NCT is the largest of the four main terminals for loading and unloading containers at the port. The process of handing over the terminal to a foreign operator was initiated under the previous government and later resumed by the interim government.
The new BNP government recently instructed the Chittagong Port Authority to continue negotiations with DP World, leading to the finalization of the deal.
The government maintains that the partnership will increase operational efficiency, speed up container handling through modern technology, and attract foreign direct investment.
However, the deal has faced strong opposition from several leftist political parties and the Port Protection Committee. Protesters held a sit-in outside the auditorium during the signing ceremony.
Opponents argue that handing over the terminal to a foreign operator could lead to revenue losses, weaken the skilled local workforce, and expose Bangladesh to geopolitical risks.
The Port Protection Committee has previously held mass hunger strikes and protest marches, demanding that the leasing process be scrapped entirely.
caption:
Dubai's DP World will now operate Chittagong Port's largest container terminal despite widespread protests.

The new BNP government recently instructed the Chittagong Port Authority to continue negotiations with DP World, leading to the finalization of the deal.

The government maintains that the partnership will increase operational efficiency, speed up container handling through modern technology, and attract foreign direct investment.

However, the deal has faced strong opposition from several leftist political parties and the Port Protection Committee. Protesters held a sit-in outside the auditorium during the signing ceremony.

Opponents argue that handing over the terminal to a foreign operator could lead to revenue losses, weaken the skilled local workforce, and expose Bangladesh to geopolitical risks.

headline: 1,144 dead as measles outbreak death toll rises
summary: Four more people have died in the last 24 hours as the measles crisis continues to claim lives.
details: A measles outbreak has resulted in a total of 1,144 deaths. The situation has escalated rapidly, with four more deaths reported in the last 24 hours.
The surge in fatalities highlights the severity of the outbreak and the urgent need for medical intervention and vaccination efforts to curb the spread of the virus.
